<pasted_content id="d864">
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

Use Unsplash for images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.
</pasted_content id="d864">

finalReport:
The blog is built and working: all three pages return 200, every block renders through its ViewComponent, and all images load.

## What I built

**Content model (over MCP)**
- **Blocks:** `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock` and `blogPostListBlock`, all filed in the Blocks folder.
- **Data type:** `Blog Block Grid`, a 12-column grid allowing those five blocks.
- **Pages:** `blogFrontPage` and `blogPost`, in the Pages folder, each with a `blocks` grid and its own template.
- **Site root:** `siteRoot` now allows `blogFrontPage` as a child.

**Content (over MCP)**
- **Front page:** "MCP Notes" under WWW with domain `/`, made of a hero, an intro text and the post list.
- **Post 1:** "MCP Is the USB-C Port for AI" (22 September 2026).
- **Post 2:** "This Blog Was Built Without Opening the Backoffice" (29 September 2026).
- **Media:** five Unsplash images in a `Blog` media folder.

**Code (after the restart)**
- Plain view models in [Models/Blocks/](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Models/Blocks/)
- One ViewComponent per block in [ViewComponents/](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/ViewComponents/), with views in [Views/Shared/Components/](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/Shared/Components/)
- Adapter partials named by element alias in [Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/)
- [_Layout.cshtml](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml), [blogFrontPage.cshtml](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml) and [blogPost.cshtml](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/blogPost.cshtml), which render blocks with `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`
- Block grid layout and rich text styles in [site.css](Umbraco.Bench.Frontend/src/site.css)

## How to view it

Umbraco is running now, started from this session.

| Page | URL |
|---|---|
| Front page | https://localhost:44317/ |
| Post 1 | https://localhost:44317/mcp-is-the-usb-c-port-for-ai/ |
| Post 2 | https://localhost:44317/this-blog-was-built-without-opening-the-backoffice/ |
| Backoffice | https://localhost:44317/umbraco (admin@example.com / 1234567890) |

If the site has stopped, run `dotnet run` in `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco`.

## Things to know

- **Not everything is a block.** The post's excerpt, list image, publish date and author are page properties, because the post list needs them. The post template also renders the date, author and "All posts" link outside the grid.
- **The CSS bundle is a one-off build.** I ran `npm install` and `npm run build` in `Umbraco.Bench.Frontend`. If you change Tailwind classes in a view, rebuild or run `npm run watch`.
- **`ViewComponents/` is a new folder.** AGENTS.md doesn't say where ViewComponent classes live, so I put them at the project root.
- **Images uploaded by URL get a left-edge focal point.** `create-media` set the focal point to `left: 0`, which crops off-centre. I reset all five to centre and removed `.jpg` from their names with `update-media`.
- **The post list block is allowed on posts too.** There is one grid data type for both page types, so an editor could add the list to a post.

Nothing is broken that I know of; the log shows no errors or warnings beyond the standard application URL notice.
